sources.locator: React Learn and Reference; React 19.2; provisions applicable to Custom hooks for reusable logic
sources.claim: A custom hook packages reusable stateful logic and other hooks while each caller receives independent state unless an external store is shared.

canonicalExplanation.summary: A **custom hook** is a function whose name starts with `use` and that calls other hooks, packaging **reusable stateful logic**: a subscription, a fetch, a timer. `useOnlineStatus()` can set up the online/offline listeners, clean them up, and return `true` or `false`. Each component that calls it gets **its own independent state and effects**, because hooks share *logic*, not *data*. If two components must share the same live value, it has to come from something outside them, such as the browser, a context or a store, which here is the browser's own online flag.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A lesson player shows an "offline" banner, and the save button also needs to know when the learner is offline. Both components copy the same 15 lines of listener code, and one copy forgets to remove its listeners. useOnlineStatus owns one subscription pattern and cleans it up for each consuming component. In this lesson you'll design and test a focused custom hook used by two components.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Cleanup and race prevention**, **Fetch and HTTP responses**, **Client fetch lifecycle**, and **Dependencies and reactive values**, since hooks contain effects.

examples.title: One online-status hook, two components
examples.situation: useOnlineStatus owns one subscription pattern and cleans it up for each consuming component.
walkthrough: **Extract:** the copied listener code moves into useOnlineStatus, which returns isOnline.
**Clean up for each consuming component:** every caller adds its own listeners and removes the same functions on unmount.
**Test:** render OfflineBanner and SaveButton, fire an offline event, and a test will see the banner text and a disabled Offline button.
examples.result: Both components react to connection changes, and no listeners are left behind when either unmounts.

examples.title: The hook that was meant to share
examples.situation: A team writes `useCart()` with useState inside and calls it in the header and the checkout page, expecting both to show the same items. Adding an item on checkout doesn't update the header.
walkthrough: Each call created its own cart state.
Custom hooks don't share data between callers.
Fix: keep the cart in a CartProvider (context + reducer) and have useCart read from that context.
examples.result: The header and checkout show the same cart because it lives in one provider.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Calling the same custom hook in two components automatically shares one state instance.
misconceptions.correction: Every call to a custom hook runs its hooks again for that component, creating separate state and effects. To share one value, store it outside: context, a store, or an external source.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The hook that was meant to share", why didn't the header update?

analogy.example: A custom hook is like **a recipe card**: many kitchens can cook from it, and each gets its own dish. If you want everyone to eat from **the same pot**, you need a shared pot (context or a store), not more copies of the recipe.
limitations: Recipes don't subscribe to anything; hooks can, and each copy cleans up its own.
Two kitchens reading the same thermometer (navigator.onLine) will agree without sharing a pot.

farTransfer.prompt: Extract a `useLessonSearch(query)` hook with fetch, abort, status and retry from an existing component. Use it in two places and test the hook through a small test component, including out-of-order responses.

remediation.explanation: Before writing a hook ask: **What one question does it answer?** Name it for that. After writing it ask: **Does each caller need its own state, or one shared value?** If shared, add a provider.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The hook that was meant to share".

recap.summary: To design and test a focused custom hook, move reusable stateful logic into a use-named function that sets up and cleans up its own effects and returns simple values. Each component that calls it gets independent state; share one value through context, a store or an external source instead.
